decisions.reason: As a prominently launched extension of the firm's core psychiatric treatment pathway, it carries high strategic fit and visible prior commitment, so management is very likely to continue and interpret any issues as temporary.

The standalone presentation and the firm's rehabilitation and production capabilities create enough sunk commitment and justificatory pressure that management would probably retain the workshop rather than reverse course now.
Even with lower public visibility, outpatient sociotherapy is close to the firm's person-centered core services, which supports continued commitment after the initial investment.

This is still the most peripheral and least prominently committed offer, but because it builds on sheltered workshop activities and has already been kept once, management is more likely to persist than to shut it down.

As a newly introduced service that fits the firm's senior support portfolio, management would likely give it more time and attribute any early underperformance to startup effects rather than withdraw quickly.
